items.summary: Board President Rafael Mandelman called the regular meeting to order, followed by the roll call and land acknowledgment. All eleven supervisors were present. Supervisor Jackie Fielder was granted privilege of the floor to address her colleagues and the public upon returning from an extended medical leave.

speakers.name: Jackie Fielder
speakers.quote: I WANT TO THANK YOU FOR YOUR GRACE IN EXTENDING A EXCUSE FOR MY ABSENCE FOR AN EXTENDED LEAVE. IT'S NOT SOMETHING THAT I WANTED TO DO BUT SOMETHING THAT MY DOCTOR RECOMMENDED AND I'M VERY GLAD I DID TAKE THE TIME TO PROTECT MY MENTAL HEALTH.

items.summary: The Clerk of the Board announced instructions for public participation, broadcast channels, written comment submissions, and accommodation requests under the Americans with Disabilities Act.
The Board considered the consent agenda consisting of Items 1 through 4, which included four litigation settlements. The items were approved unanimously on a roll call vote.

The Board approved four routine settlements on the consent agenda: Cruz and Jimenez ($3,000,000), Kennedy-Phelps ($50,000), Williams ($35,000), and unlitigated claim Banks ($100,000). The ordinances passed on first reading and the resolution was adopted unanimously.

The Board considered an ordinance amending the Administrative Code regarding the Domestic Violence Shelter-Based Program Fund, transferring administrative duties to the Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development and aligning local provisions with state law. The ordinance was finally passed without objection.

The Board considered a 308-page code cleanup ordinance removing obsolete reporting requirements, defunct funds, and inactive programs across various municipal codes. Multiple supervisors voiced concerns regarding legislative transparency, community outreach, and specific reporting eliminations. The Board voted without objection to continue the item for two weeks to July 14, 2026.

items.summary: The Board considered an ordinance amending the Fair Chance Ordinance in the Police Code to prohibit employers and affordable housing providers from using out-of-state convictions or arrests for reproductive health care, gender-affirming care, and drug-related conduct that is lawful in California. The ordinance was passed on first reading without objection.

The Board considered a resolution authorizing the Mayor or a designee to cast an assessment ballot in favor of the renewal and expansion of the Downtown Community Benefit District for city-owned parcels. The resolution was adopted without objection.
The Board adopted a resolution approving the San Francisco Police Department's 2025 Annual Report on Law Enforcement Equipment Use Policy, pursuant to state law requirements.

The Board debated a proposed charter amendment for the November 2026 ballot to establish a Municipal Finance Corporation and public bank framework. Proponents emphasized expanded access to capital for small businesses and affordable housing, while opponents raised concerns about financial risk and municipal capacity amid a budget deficit. A motion to continue the item to July 7, 2026, passed 10-1, with Supervisor Wong dissenting.

items.summary: The Board unanimously approved a resolution designating the 500 and 600 blocks of Connecticut Street with the commemorative street name 'Art Agnos Way' in honor of former Mayor Art Agnos.

The Board considered amendments to its Rules of Order to comply with state law (SB 707) requiring remote public comment options at full Board meetings, as well as policies governing meeting disruptions. While supervisors voiced strong frustration over potential bad-faith callers and limited local authority, the motion was adopted without objection to avoid legal liability under the Brown Act.

items.summary: Supervisors introduced new legislation and inquiries during roll call. Mandelman introduced resolutions backing AB 1573 and raising the City Attorney's settlement authority to $100,000; Melgar announced rent ordinance amendments restricting eviction grounds; Wong introduced a healthcare corridor designation for Noriega Street; Chan introduced a support resolution for KGO-TV's license renewal; and Fielder submitted an inquiry regarding SFPD deployments during Pride weekend.

Speakers criticized the administration's allocation of Prop C funds, condemned the criminalization of homelessness following the Grants Pass Supreme Court decision, denounced aggressive police tactics during Pride and the Trans March, supported the Coors boycott commemoration, and raised labor concerns for frontline healthcare staff.

items.summary: The Board considered Items 15 through 19 on the adoption without committee reference agenda. The resolutions and motions were adopted unanimously on a single roll call vote.

The Board unanimously adopted Items 15 through 19 without committee reference, including the Coors Boycott Commemoration Day resolution, the California Arts Council local partner designation, certified June 2026 election results, opposition to federal disability benefit cuts for veterans, a Committee of the Whole hearing on Kaiser Permanente bargaining, and city contract approvals.
The Board adjourned the meeting in memory of longtime Glen Park salon owner Gloria Dela Rea and retired library worker Stanislaw Chan.
